correctness.rationale: For j hypergeometric in the daughter of size a, survival is exactly 2j<=a for the small and 2j>=a for the large daughter. The explicitly derived formulas for a=1,2,3 give positive differences (m²+1)/(2(2m−1)), (m−2)/(2(2m−1)), m((m−2)²+1)/(2(2m−1)) and 2m(m−2)/(2m−1); expected-infected/expected-living differences also have strictly positive factorizations for every m>=3. Exact arithmetic independently checked m=3..149 and labeled six-cell microstates, with finite checks not used as proof of the all-m result.

value.rationale: The original work motivates two distinct one-event mechanisms of infection control: removal of severely infected daughters and reduced within-offspring infected–healthy mixing. The result isolates a parity-mediated failure of monotonically increasing purging/isolation with bottleneck asymmetry for all even parent sizes >=6 and verifies that the middle bottleneck also leaves the highest normalized expected infection burden. This is a natural model-theoretic boundary with direct diagnostic value for fragmented multicellular infection models, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
